chain.label: Clutch bearing incorrectly assembled during actuator production
chain.trigger: a clutch bearing on the upper gearbox assembly was inadvertently assembled with the seal facing toward the clutch teeth instead of the seal facing away from the clutch teeth

chain.label: Moisture entered actuator through pressure test port pinhole, migrated to bearing, and froze in flight, restricting the actuator's output crank arm
chain.trigger: moisture that previously entered the actuator through the pressure test port pinhole, migrated to the incorrectly assembled sealed bearing, and froze during flight

caused_by.evidence: Disassembly of the actuator revealed evidence of moisture within the unit, as shown in figure 2, which would account for the resistance observed in excess of specified design limits

chain.label: Rudder pedals jammed at neutral, unresponsive to pedal force during landing and rollout
chain.trigger: the rudder pedals were 'stuck' in their neutral position and did not move in response to the 'normal' application of foot pressure to maintain alignment with the runway centerline

caused_by.evidence: the rudder control system was stuck (as discovered during the landing rollout) as a result of moisture ... migrated to the incorrectly assembled sealed bearing, and froze during flight

chain.label: Crew used nosewheel steering tiller for directional control; jam cleared during taxi; airplane and occupants unharmed
chain.trigger: The captain elected instead to use the nosewheel steering tiller as the airplane slowed to a safe taxi speed ... the rudder pedals and rudder surface began to operate normally. The airplane taxied to the gate without further incident ... deplaned without any injuries or damage to the airplane

caused_by.evidence: the flight crew applied approximately 42 pounds of force to the pedals, but the jam persisted. The captain elected instead to use the nosewheel steering tiller
